classificationNotes: Source-draft Doppelgangers are treated as a copy-quality and leaking-disguise visual and encounter-production family. Claims about infiltration, motive, social behavior, cognition, agency, personhood, and hostility remain proposals pending taxonomy review.
visualConstants: A generic humanoid copy silhouette retains one deliberate flaw until layered face and mask motifs appear at explicit upper tiers.
Clay-gray skin, putty, borrowed colors, porcelain, copied cloth, and smooth flesh remain discrete source materials rather than Earth affinity.
Seams, wrong joints, ill-fitting clothes, and layered masks reveal copy quality while preserving the readable original-copy relationship.
Disguise fidelity escalates from an entirely blank true form to a sovereign carrying many stolen-looking faces at once.
escalationAxis: Copy fidelity and the number of simultaneous borrowed identities advance from blank smooth flesh to a body-wide sovereign mask procession.

constructionDimensions: Family-native, non-affinity clay-gray skin, copied colors or borrowed colors, shapeshifting, masks and faces, and smooth flesh remain source-supported body material, disguise behavior, and identity leakage—not Earth or any other affinity.
Putty, mask porcelain, borrowed cloth, seams, wrong joints, and deliberately imperfect fit preserve copy readability without elemental substitution.
normal.counterplaySignal: The established blank wrist, unfinished limb, jaw seam, rotating face edge, or mask-crown latch remains readable against the borrowed copy.
forbidden: Affinity construction that obscures which feature is copied and which remains native

Motion/process branches: T1 the blank featureless limb drives one external combustion cycle around its silhouette; T2 the partial copy sheds smoke only from its finished surface; T3 the wrong hand opens the jaw-seam vent; T4 layered faces rotate heat from one mask clasp; T5 body-wide faces ignite and cool one mask-crown latch.

forbidden: Fire effects that hide the borrowed-versus-native boundary

forms.battlefieldDuty: Probe close timing with one smooth unfinished reach from a deliberately generic stance.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach that the blank wrist briefly creases before featureless fingers extend.
forms.signatureMechanic: Unpainted Reach: one clay-gray arm lengthens without a shoulder turn, then returns through a visible wrist crease.
forms.telegraph: The smooth wrist dimples while the blank head with no face, hair, or clothing remains perfectly still.
forms.counterplay: Step across the extending arm and strike the temporary wrist crease before it smooths.
forms.visualDelta: Blank smooth gray humanoid with no face, no hair, no clothing, and an unfinished mannequin-like surface.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Repeat copied weapon pressure from a partial disguise whose one gray arm cannot complete the same motion.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach that the blurred mouth announces the copied strike while the unfinished arm remains the safe side.
forms.signatureMechanic: Half-Learned Cut: the finished side copies a simple cut as the unformed gray arm attempts and fails to mirror it.
forms.telegraph: The nearly right face blurs at the mouth and borrowed color drains toward the finished shoulder.
forms.counterplay: Cross the unfinished-arm side and punish its smooth shoulder after the copied cut.
forms.visualDelta: Half-copied form with one unformed gray arm and a nearly right face blurred at the mouth.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Blanks reach from the copied side; striking the unfinished shoulder exposes both wrist creases.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot into a reactive copy specialist that perfectly mirrors one action except for a wrong hand joint and jaw seam.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach players to offer a harmless motion, identify the anatomically impossible mirror, and attack the jaw seam during correction.
forms.signatureMechanic: One Error Copy: the near-perfect human copy mirrors the target's last committed posture, but one hand bends the wrong way and pulls a faint jaw seam open.
forms.telegraph: Borrowed clothing settles into exact symmetry while the wrong hand rotates one joint too far and the jaw seam pales.
forms.counterplay: Feed a short recoverable motion, move opposite the wrong hand, and strike the open jaw seam before the copy corrects.
forms.visualDelta: Near-perfect human copy betrayed by faint jaw seams and one hand jointed the wrong way.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Halfling Copies repeat the offered motion imperfectly; interrupting their finished side delays the Mimic's correction.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Control three alternating attack rules by rotating layered faces to the front of an otherwise flawless copy.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach that the rear mask edge moves before the next face and remains vulnerable after the transition.
forms.signatureMechanic: Front in Turn: three layered faces rotate through the front position, each calling a learned reach, cut, or mirrored response while the vacated edge stays open.
forms.telegraph: Two mask profiles slide backward and the third face becomes unnaturally still before its rule begins.
forms.counterplay: Read the incoming profile, answer its familiar rule, and strike the trailing mask edge after it rotates away.
forms.visualDelta: Flawless copy wearing three layered faces like masks, each shifting to the front in turn.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Blank, Halfling Copy, and Mimic each supply one face rule; disabling that lower form leaves its layer unable to close.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Transform a copy arena through body-wide face processions while the mask crown commands learned lower-form defects.
forms.teachingGoal: Test blank wrists, unfinished sides, wrong joints, and rotating mask edges while each removed crown mask strips one copied phase from the body.
forms.signatureMechanic: Arena Transformation — Parade of Faces: one mask-crown segment lowers, body-wide faces stream from chest to arms and back, and the sovereign copies a lower Doppelganger rule until its source defect reaches the crown latch.
forms.telegraph: Borrowed colors move across the smooth flesh, one crown mask tips forward, and the called lower-form defect appears on the last face in the procession.
forms.counterplay: Answer the announced copied rule and strike the crown latch when its source defect arrives; each removed mask erases one procession and reveals more blank native flesh.
forms.visualDelta: Shifting parade of stolen-looking faces across chest, arms, and back beneath a crown made of masks.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Blank, Halfling Copy, Mimic, and Facewearer each define one mask-crown phase; solving its defect exposes the linked latch.
